domain: Observatory chronometer trials (Greenwich, Neuchatel, Kew, Geneva, Besancon): sealed rival instruments run side by side under one published programme of temperature and position, judged on variation of rate rather than best rate, scored by a published trial formula, certified by bulletin de marche with residuals, with premiums withheld when nothing clears threshold, a discrimination limit set by the standard clock's own error, the documented trial-tuned instrument that fails at sea, and re-rating after transport or repair
axioms: A submitted rate sheet is re-examined - conditions, arithmetic, provenance - before its numbers are admitted into any comparison.
One chamber, one published programme: arms observed under different conditions cannot be compared, and a conditions mismatch invalidates rather than caveats the comparison.
Consistency across the programme is the judged quantity; best-case showing is not.
The apparatus has its own error, so there exists a discrimination limit below which two entrants cannot honestly be ordered; declared ties are correct output and invented orderings are a defect.
Withholding the award is a normal verdict: the null wins whenever no entrant clears a threshold stated in advance.
Submitters tune to the published programme; a measure that can be gamed will be, and this is a predictable force to design against rather than misconduct to deplore.
A certificate is a statement about a particular instrument in a particular period, so it carries its own re-rating trigger and revocation condition.
Class certificates are awarded within class, so entrants are compared as class winners rather than by entrant count.
primitives: trial entrant (sealed submission) and trial arm
published programme (temperature cycles, positions) = matched conditions
mean daily rate vs variation of rate
trial number / scoring formula and its resolution floor
standard clock error and the discrimination limit
bulletin de marche: observed behaviour plus residuals
failure_mode: Cannot judge semantic novelty at all: two entrants that behave identically under the programme are indistinguishable to it, even if one embodies a genuinely new operation and the other is a renaming.

Its authority depends on a programme existing; where conditions cannot be matched or a candidate's value only appears outside any runnable programme, it will systematically under-rate rather than acknowledge the blind spot.
Conservative by construction - it withholds under uncertainty, so it will miss a real but not-yet-measurable improvement and will under-reward candidates whose payoff is long-horizon or qualitative.
Prices measurable behaviour and ignores learnability, naming, mnemonic economy, and the human cost of operating a design.
Treats entrants as sealed, independent, and interchangeable, so it is blind to interaction effects between candidates and to topology or composition effects when several are adopted together.
Assumes a single scalar-ish verdict per class; genuinely multi-dimensional or conditional recommendations strain its certificate format and may get flattened.
